title: CORS allows any origin with credentials
description: server.rs:29-33. The CorsLayer is configured with allow_origin(Any), allow_methods(Any), allow_headers(Any), expose_headers(Any). This allows any website to make credentialed requests to the API. While axum/tower-http's CorsLayer with Any origin will NOT set Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true (it only reflects the origin when credentials are allowed), the overly broad CORS policy still allows any website to read public API responses (instance metadata, public posts, etc). For a fediverse server this is expected behavior, but it would also allow any website to perform authenticated requests if the browser sends cookies — though smallhold uses Bearer tokens, not cookies, so this is mitigated.
close_reason: CORS Any is standard for Mastodon-compatible APIs. Clients like Elk, Phanpy, Ivory run on different origins. Bearer token auth means cookies are not at risk.
